Change c0543. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): I was nourished with high thoughts of honour and devotion.

1818 text: But now vice has degraded me beneath the meanest animal. No crime, no mischief, no malignity, no misery, can be found comparable to mine. When I call over the frightful catalogue of my deeds, I cannot believe that I am he whose thoughts were once filled with sublime and transcendant visions of the beauty and the majesty of goodness.

1831 text: But now crime has degraded me beneath the meanest animal. No guilt, no mischief, no malignity, no misery, can be found comparable to mine. When I run over the frightful catalogue of my sins, I cannot believe that I am the same creature whose thoughts were once filled with sublime and transcendent visions of the beauty and the majesty of goodness.

Diff: But now [-vice-] {+crime+} has degraded me beneath the meanest animal. No [-crime-] {+guilt+} , no mischief, no malignity, no misery, can be found comparable to mine. When I [-call-] {+run+} over the frightful catalogue of my [-deeds-] {+sins+} , I cannot believe that I am [-he-] {+the same creature+} whose thoughts were once filled with sublime and [-transcendant-] {+transcendent+} visions of the beauty and the majesty of goodness.

Context after (unchanged): But it is even so; the fallen angel becomes a malignant devil.

result.rationale: Replacing 'vice' and 'deeds' with 'crime' and 'sins', and 'crime' with 'guilt', shifts the creature's self-judgment from behaviour to moral sinfulness and guilt, a religious register that frames his wrongdoing as sin.
